question: Under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita(BNSS), what is the maximum period for which a person can be held in police custody in total, even if remanded periodically by a magistrate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**15 days (for initial remand, extendable)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)** governs various provisions related to criminal proceedings in India, replacing the earlier Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC).
 
• Under BNSS, a person can be held in **police custody for an initial period of 15 days**. This period can be extended periodically if the magistrate approves such extensions.
 
• The **magistrate has the authority** to grant extensions beyond the initial 15 days, but the cumulative period of police custody cannot exceed the prescribed limits.
 
• As per BNSS, **police custody is limited to 15 days at a time**, ensuring judicial oversight to prevent misuse of custodial provisions.
 
• This provision ensures that the rights of individuals are protected while allowing the police sufficient time to conduct investigations. Hence, option "15 days (for initial remand, extendable)" is c
